clue.text: Experimental version of Bible, different and great

indicators.note: words made different are changed into another form, so their letters get rearranged

parts.note: the Authorised Version of the Bible is abbreviated AV
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a daring new edition of the Bible, hoping it will be different and great.
explanation.walkthrough: The Authorised Version, or King James Bible, is the standard English translation, hence AV.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-garde art is innovative and boundary-pushing, so it is a close synonym for experimental work.

clue.text: Roguish star charismatic in part

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the solution sits inside a run of letters

parts.note: the last two letters of the first word plus the first two of the second

explanation.surface: A charming film star is partly a lovable rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a knowingly playful, mischievous manner, much like roguish teasing.

clue.text: Notice, before speech, habit that's hard to break

indicators.note: one thing coming before another fixes the order of the two parts in the answer

parts.note: an advertisement, or ad, is a public notice
diction is one's manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A notice put up ahead of a talk about a habit people struggle to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependency, which is exactly a habit one finds very difficult to stop.

clue.text: Huge long stain ruined carpeting

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are put back in another order

parts.note: thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A big, lengthy stain has spoiled the carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' looks like floor covering, but in British English to carpet someone is to reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpeting is a British informal term for a severe scolding, which a tongue-lashing also is.

clue.text: Spy cheers up, receiving information

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one part holds the other inside
in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A spy celebrates, raising a glass, on getting intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is an operative working covertly for a government, a common synonym for a spy.

clue.text: Waterbirds, unknown quantity, full of appeal and variety

indicators.note: a thing full of something has it inside, so one part goes within the others

parts.note: divers are diving water birds, also called loons
it means sex appeal, as in an 'It girl'
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: Water birds of uncertain number provide charm and variety to a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversity is a range of different things, which is what variety means.

clue.text: Projection from type of poker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small knob or boss sticking out of a surface
second meaning: a card game where some cards are dealt face up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something sticking out of a fireplace poker; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a raised knob on a surface and a well-known form of poker.

clue.text: Deal with indulgence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to handle or behave towards
second meaning: a special pleasure one allows oneself

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a phrase about tolerating something; it is two separate meanings of one word, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to handle someone or something; as a noun it is a pleasurable luxury.

clue.text: Democrat, terribly sorry, idle and undisciplined

indicators.note: doing something terribly means doing it badly, so the following letters end up jumbled

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat
nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A US politician is very apologetic for being lazy and unruly.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorderly behaviour is unruly and lacking control, the same as undisciplined conduct.

clue.text: Rhythm found by trainee endlessly going round enclosure

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one part wraps the other
without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or police
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure, as at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A trainee walking endless laps around a pen settles into a rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclosure' suggests a pen or paddock, but here it is the abbreviation written on letters with something attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is the rise and fall or beat of sound or movement, a synonym for rhythm.

clue.text: Service involves persuasion to some extent

indicators.note: the clue words involve the solution, meaning it sits within them
only part of the phrase is used, pointing to a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the end of the first indicator word runs into the start of this word

explanation.surface: Providing a service partly depends on persuading people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap: the tail of 'involves' and the head of 'persuasion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening church service of prayer, so it is an example of a service.

clue.text: Words of love, unconvincing in wetness, go awry

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
things gone awry are out of place, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: a thin excuse is a weak, unconvincing one
nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Romantic murmurings sound unconvincing when rain spoils the date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconvincing' is a separate piece, slipped into the rearranged letters of the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet nothings are the affectionate, trivial things lovers whisper to each other.

clue.text: Creator of forgery caught by altering one fruit tree

indicators.note: altering things changes them, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
twelve letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A forger is arrested for tampering with an orchard tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterfeiter makes fakes, especially false money, so is someone who produces forgeries.

clue.text: Easily controlled, gripped by craze, not at home

indicators.note: something gripped by another is held inside it

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze
to run a business is to control it
someone away is out, not at home

explanation.surface: Someone easily led by a passing craze is never at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easily' looks like an adverb describing the control; it is the definition, as in winning easily.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means by a large margin, as when one is clearly the best, which is to win easily.

clue.text: Playing Lear, I will show Shakespearian spirit

indicators.note: playing with things moves them around, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor boasts that in the role of King Lear he will reveal a Shakespearean spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing Lear' suggests acting the role; Lear is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Appear to grasp full amount, ignoring a philosopher

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: to arise is to appear or come into being

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a total is the full amount
the letter to be left out

explanation.surface: A thinker seems to understand everything except one small detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Reptile having problem climbing into a good area on hill

indicators.note: going into something puts one part inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good
A is the abbreviation for area
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: an ill is a trouble or problem

explanation.surface: A reptile struggles to clamber up into a nice spot on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hilltop, a word common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An alligator is a large crocodilian, a type of reptile.

clue.text: Bad informer in dreadful dither

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
something dreadful is a mess, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: a rat is someone who informs on associates
six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor informant is in a terrible state of indecision.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means of low quality, inferior, which is an everyday sense of bad.

clue.text: Target provided by colleague, after jibes, having time off

indicators.note: one part coming after another sets the order of the two pieces
something taken off is removed, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taunts are jibes or jeers
T is the abbreviation for time; this is the letter removed
an ally is a partner or associate

explanation.surface: A workmate becomes the butt of teasing after taking leave.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British fairground and pub game in which sticks are thrown at a dummy's head; figuratively, an easy target.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aunt Sally is a person or idea set up as an object of criticism, a target for attack.

clue.text: Window that is large, with nothing right in front

indicators.note: parts in front come first, so they are placed ahead of the rest

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
R is the abbreviation for right
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big window with nothing in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey, so it is a kind of window.

clue.text: Eminent inspector — smart, upper-class one — lost

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks
to smart is to sting with pain
U is the British label for upper-class usage
I is the Roman numeral for one
to shed something is to lose it, as leaves or weight

explanation.surface: A well-dressed, posh police inspector has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as well dressed; here it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished means renowned and respected, a synonym for eminent.

clue.text: Clean comb

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a tidy comb; both words are verbs, one for scrubbing and one for searching.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to scrub a surface vigorously and to search an area exhaustively.

clue.text: Elected, raised support for republic

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help or support

explanation.surface: Newly elected leaders raise backing for a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a federal parliamentary republic in South Asia, so it is an example of a republic.

clue.text: Singular outfit for piece of satire

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
kit is a set of clothing or gear

explanation.surface: An odd costume worn for a satirical performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like 'odd'; it is the grammatical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch, typically one that parodies or satirises something.

clue.text: Made western violent, ending in shoot-out

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
rough play is violent

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A violent cowboy film culminating in a gunfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' suggests a cowboy film; it is only the compass abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrought is an old past participle of work, meaning made or fashioned, as in wrought iron.

clue.text: Study sign in country

parts.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
a mark is a sign or symbol

explanation.surface: Researching the symbols used in a particular nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Denmark is a Scandinavian nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Diamonds gleam around enclosed area

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
a ray is a gleam or beam of light

explanation.surface: Diamonds sparkle all around a walled courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is a piece of ground enclosed by walls or buildings, such as a courtyard.

clue.text: Newspaper's ways followed by man dividing opinion

indicators.note: something dividing another splits it in two, so it sits inside it

parts.note: 'my bet is' means 'in my opinion'

indicators.note: one part followed by another fixes the order in which they join

parts.note: roads are ways
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A newspaper's routes, plus a man who divides public opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: A broadsheet is a large-format paper, traditionally associated with serious British dailies.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a newspaper printed on large pages, as opposed to a tabloid.
